subject: physics
title: Work done and energy transfer
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Work done and energy transfer — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.5.2.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Work done and energy transfer, specification section 4.5.2.
final_note: You worked through Work done and energy transfer — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: Work is done on an object when a force causes the object to move through a distance, that is when the force causes a displacement of the object. A force that produces no displacement does no work, however large the force is and however long it is applied for.

concepts.term: Distance moved along the line of action of the force
concepts.def: The distance s used in the work equation is the distance the object moves along the line of action of the force, not simply any distance it travels. Movement at right angles to the force contributes nothing to the work done by that force.

work done = force × distance (moved along the line of action of the force), written in symbols as W = F s, where work done, W, is in joules, J; force, F, is in newtons, N; and distance, s, is in metres.
The unit of work done and of energy. One joule of work is done when a force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre.

Force in newtons multiplied by distance in metres gives work in newton-metres. The newton-metre and the joule are the same size of unit: 1 joule = 1 newton-metre, so a value in N m converts to the identical number of J.

concepts.term: Energy transfer when work is done
concepts.def: Doing work is a way of transferring energy. When a force does work on an object, energy is transferred to that object, and the amount of energy transferred in joules is equal to the work done in joules.
When an object moves against frictional forces, work is done against those forces. The energy transferred is not lost: it raises the temperature of the object rather than making it move faster.

Work done against the frictional forces acting on an object causes a rise in the temperature of the object, so surfaces such as brake blocks, rubbed hands and dragged crates become warmer as they move.

mcqs.q: In which of these situations is work done on the object by the force described?
options: A sledge is dragged forwards and slides 5 m over snow
A cleaner pushes hard on a crate that does not move
A waiter carries a tray level across a room
A student holds a bag of books still for a minute
mcqs.explain: The pulling force causes a displacement of the sledge along its own line of action, so work is done on the sledge.

mcqs.q: A student holds a box of weight 40 N still at chest height for 15 s. How much work does the student's upward force do on the box?
options: 0 J
mcqs.explain: The box has no displacement, so s = 0 and W = 40 × 0 = 0 J.

mcqs.q: In the equation work done = force × distance, what is meant by the distance?
options: The total length of the path that the object takes
The distance the object moves, in any direction
The distance moved along the line of action of the force
The time for which the force carries on acting
mcqs.explain: The specification defines the distance as the distance moved along the line of action of the force.

mcqs.q: A force of 25 N pushes a trolley 8 m along the line of action of the force. How much work is done on the trolley?
options: 3.125 joules
0.32 joules
33 joules
200 joules
mcqs.explain: W = F s = 25 × 8 = 200 J, with the distance measured along the line of action of the force.

mcqs.q: A crane does 3000 J of work on a load using a force of 250 N. How far does the load move along the line of action of the force?
mcqs.explain: Rearranging W = F s gives s = W ÷ F = 3000 ÷ 250 = 12 m.

mcqs.q: Which row gives the correct units for the quantities in W = F s?
options: work in newtons, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in joules, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in watts, force in newtons, distance in metres
work in joules, force in newtons, time in seconds
mcqs.explain: Work done, W, in joules, J; force, F, in newtons, N; distance, s, in metres.

mcqs.q: A motor does 6000 N m of work. What is this work done in joules?
options: 6 J
mcqs.explain: 1 joule = 1 newton-metre, so the number is unchanged: 6000 N m = 6000 J.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly defines one joule of work?
options: The work done when a force of 1 N acts for a time of 1 s
The force of 1 N needed to move an object through 1 m
The work done when 1 N of energy is given to a body
The work done when a force of 1 N causes a displacement of 1 m
mcqs.explain: This is the specification definition: one joule of work is done when a force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre.

mcqs.q: A crane lifts a steel beam steadily upwards. Which statement best describes what happens as the crane's force does work on the beam?
options: Energy is transferred to the beam by the crane's force
New energy is created by the crane and passed to the beam
Energy is used up by the crane, so none reaches it
Force is stored inside the beam as it is lifted
mcqs.explain: Doing work is a way of transferring energy; the joules of work done equal the joules transferred to the beam.

mcqs.q: A crate is pushed at a steady speed across a rough floor. What is the main effect of the work done against the frictional forces on the crate?
options: The energy transferred is destroyed by friction
The temperature of the crate rises steadily
The kinetic energy of the crate keeps rising
The friction only slows the crate down
mcqs.explain: Work done against the frictional forces acting on an object causes a rise in the temperature of the object.

mcqs.q: A student rubs their hands together quickly and the hands become warmer. Which statement best explains this?
options: The movement energy is used up and lost as heat
Warm air trapped between the hands heats them
Work is done against friction at the hands
New heat energy is made by the rubbing
mcqs.explain: Work done against the frictional forces acting on the hands causes a rise in their temperature.

mcqs.q: A force does 250 J of work on a trailer as the trailer is pulled along a track. What does this tell you?
options: 250 J of new energy was created by the pulling
250 J of energy was used up and cannot return
A force of 250 N acted on the trailer as it moved
250 J of energy has been transferred to it
mcqs.explain: The work done by a force equals the energy it transfers, so the trailer gained 250 J.
